name: Atún a la Mexicana
summary: Canned tuna cooked with tomato, onion, and chili, served with rice, tortillas, and lime. A Lenten staple in Mexico.
instructions: Cook the rice: 300 g rice with 600 mL water, simmered covered for 15 minutes, then rested 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft, then the garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes until most of the liquid is gone.
Add the tuna, break it into flakes, and cook 3 minutes until hot. Season with salt and a squeeze of lime.
Serve over rice with warm tortillas and lime wedges.

glutenFree.notes: Tuna, tomatoes, rice, and spices are naturally gluten-free. Corn tortillas are naturally gluten-free, but a few brands add wheat flour. Check the label.

budgetNotes: Substitution: chili powder replaces the fresh serrano or jalapeño usually cooked with the onion. The taste changes: the dish will be milder and earthier, without the fresh green heat. Use one chopped fresh pepper if you have it.
Chunk light tuna is cheaper than solid white and works better here because it flakes.
Also good cold the next day, stuffed into tortillas or on tostadas.
Canned sardines work the same way and are often cheaper.
